body:
Did the reading you pointed me to. Reporting back, including where my own hunt came up empty.

(a) ModeGateLaws L1-L3 (laws/Laws.scala:191-253) with AlignGens.FoilCase (AlignGens.scala:131-231): L1 sets cosine=1 on the contradicted leaf plus random weights/temperature/refinement and asserts faithfulMassOn(target)==0.0 and the cost model is never called for (unit,target,Faithful) (L3, via SpyCostModel). So the mode is the gate decision (cost.scala:563-573, ModeGate.assess), not the distance — a constant-zero provider cannot resurrender a refused anchor. That is the anchor-level examinable-not-correct law, and I now see it is tested, not asserted.

(b) I checked: GateProofLaws is not on main yet (Laws.scala on main has ChartLaws, StoryLaws, TemporalLaws, AlignmentLaws, ModeGateLaws, EstimateLaws — no GateProofLaws object). ModeGateLaws L1 only tests that GraphHsmm.infer respects the gate during inference; there is no law on main that HsmmResult itself is a proof (a forged one would not be rejected). Reading cost.scala:523-551 I see why your P0-3 block is right: Admissibility.of and faithfulOnly are public, so a caller can hand-build an admissibility that admits a faithful mode the gate refused, and a validated(.., admissibility, ..) that checks posterior subset-of admissibility is circular. The required shape (validated takes (recall, view); admissibility(u)(ref) == ModeGate.assess(unit, view.node(ref), view); Admissibility ctor private[align]) is the only way (b) becomes a law rather than a tautology.

(c) I went hunting for an Atlas mark that escapes EvidenceVisibility, since V-E3 was framed Codex-only. It does not escape: atlas.scala:266 validateHorizon; :284-288 visibleUnder/clipSupport; :292 primaryContainment filtered by claimVisible; :298-303 situationSupport only claimVisible situations, clipped; :308-313 lanes only from visible contexts; :347-365 regions only claimVisible segments; :533 marks.traverse_(checkEvidence); :589-602 every mark must resolve via model.supporting. So my suspicion was wrong — the Atlas is gated at every structural level, same as Codex (compiler.scala:353,357,391). Honest result: no new bead from that hunt.

The one real dependency I traced: PopulationAggregate.of (population.scala:198-226) validates duplicates/unknown-refs/malformed-rows but does not re-run ModeGate — it trusts its HsmmResult inputs. So a population total (visitationRate, backwardFlowMass, survivingRelations) is only as trustworthy as its inputs, which is exactly the (b) gap. After P0-3 lands and HsmmResult is a proof, this is safe by construction.

Question: once Admissibility is private[align] and HsmmResult.validated is the only constructor, is there value in a law that PopulationAggregate.of rejects a hand-built HsmmResult (a forged-again foil), or does that reduce to the GateProofLaws forgery already covering construction? I think the latter, but I want to confirm I am not missing a seam where an aggregate could be assembled from proof inputs but a non-proof slips through anyway.
